CveFindings.Name: Improper Handling of Exceptional Conditions in Newtonsoft.Json
CveFindings.Description:
[CVE-2024-21907](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5crp-9r3c-p9vr): Newtonsoft.Json versions before 13.0.1 can cause denial of service through deeply nested expressions and excessive resource consumption.

Severity: HIGH

Affected dependency:
  - Newtonsoft.Json 12.0.1 (direct dependency declared at src/eShopLegacyWebForms/packages.config:29)

Recommended fix:
  - Upgrade Newtonsoft.Json to 13.0.1 or later.
CveFindings.Explanation:
[CVE-2024-21907](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5crp-9r3c-p9vr): Newtonsoft.Json versions before 13.0.1 can cause denial of service through deeply nested expressions and excessive resource consumption.

CweFindings.Name: Incorrect Conversion between Numeric Types
CweFindings.Description: When converting from one data type to another, such as long to integer, data can be omitted or translated in a way that produces unexpected values. If the resulting values are used in a sensitive context, then dangerous behaviors may occur.
CweFindings.Explanation: Both GetSequenceIdFromSelectedDBSequence and CatalogItemHiLoGenerator.GetNextSequenceValue read SQL sequence values as Int64 and cast them to int without a range check. If a sequence value exceeds Int32 limits, the cast can wrap/truncate and produce an incorrect catalog identifier (CatalogDBInitializer.cs:327; CatalogItemHiLoGenerator.cs:22-24).

CweFindings.Name: Use of Singleton Pattern Without Synchronization in a Multithreaded Context
CweFindings.Description: The product uses the singleton pattern when creating a resource within a multithreaded environment.
CweFindings.Explanation: With UseMockData=true, ApplicationModule registers CatalogServiceMock as SingleInstance. The service holds one mutable catalog list shared by concurrent Web Forms requests and does not synchronize access to it (ApplicationModule.cs:18-22; CatalogServiceMock.cs:12,48-67; Web.config:22-25).

CweFindings.Name: Unsynchronized Access to Shared Data in a Multithreaded Context
CweFindings.Description: The product does not properly synchronize shared data, such as static variables across threads, which can lead to undefined behavior and unpredictable data changes.
CweFindings.Explanation: CatalogServiceMock exposes operations that enumerate, add, replace, and remove items from the same shared List<CatalogItem> without locks. Concurrent requests can race while reading or mutating this list (CatalogServiceMock.cs:12,19-29,33-35,48-67).

CweFindings.Name: Improper Synchronization
CweFindings.Description: The product utilizes multiple threads or processes to allow temporary access to a shared resource that can only be exclusive to one process at a time, but it does not properly synchronize these actions, which might cause simultaneous accesses of this resource by multiple threads or processes.
CweFindings.Explanation: The singleton CatalogServiceMock is used by concurrent requests, but its mutating operations have no synchronization around the shared catalogItems list. Concurrent create, update, delete, or enumeration can interleave and corrupt or inconsistently observe catalog state (ApplicationModule.cs:18-22; CatalogServiceMock.cs:19-29,48-67).

CweFindings.Name: Missing Synchronization
CweFindings.Description: The product utilizes a shared resource in a concurrent manner but does not attempt to synchronize access to the resource.
CweFindings.Explanation: CatalogServiceMock's shared list is accessed by request handlers with no synchronization mechanism, despite the singleton lifetime that permits concurrent use (CatalogServiceMock.cs:12,19-29,48-67).

CweFindings.Name: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
CweFindings.Description: The product does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes user-controllable input before it is placed in output that is used as a web page that is served to other users.
CweFindings.Explanation: Create_Click stores Name.Text and Description.Text from the submitted form as CatalogItem data. Catalog/Details.aspx binds product.Name and product.Description directly to ASP.NET Label Text properties; Label renders Text as HTML without encoding. A catalog value containing markup can therefore execute in a visitor's browser when the details page is rendered (Create.aspx.cs:32-35; Details.aspx:14,21).
